discovery: The X-ray free-electron laser: theory and realization of self-amplified spontaneous emission (SASE) at short wavelengths

nominees.name: Claudio Pellegrini
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Los Angeles, and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Kwang-Je Kim
nominees.affiliation: Argonne National Laboratory and University of Chicago, USA

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / accelerator-based light sources
motivation: Pellegrini proposed, and with Kim developed the theory of, high-gain self-amplified spontaneous emission that turns a relativistic electron beam into a coherent X-ray laser without mirrors. Rossbach led the decisive TESLA Test Facility/FLASH experiments that first demonstrated SASE saturation at short wavelengths, paving the way for LCLS, SACLA, European XFEL and SwissFEL. These sources deliver X-ray pulses a billion times brighter than synchrotrons and only femtoseconds long, making visible what no one could see before: atomic-resolution structures of proteins that do not crystallize well, molecular movies of chemical reactions, matter at extreme conditions, and now attosecond X-ray pulses probing core-electron dynamics. Born of curiosity-driven accelerator and laser physics and realized through large international collaborations, the X-ray FEL has become an indispensable tool across physics, chemistry, materials science and life science, and stands as one of the great light-source inventions of our era.
